chapter: Life in New York in the 1940s
title: Weight and Basie's advice not to play on a full stomach
summary: Edison jokes about his weight and recalls Basie telling him he could not play after eating, which proved untrue.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Listen, don't you want to have something?
No, no, I'd rather sit here.
Well, you were talking about breakfast. I don't mind, you have something.
Oh, I've had coffee and grapefruit juice. And I'm trying to lose some of this weight anyway. But I feel fine.
No, it's not bad. But I gain weight right in the middle.
Right in the middle, you know. And that's a vulnerable spot after you get such an age, right in the middle.
Your muscles, you know. Hangs out.
Oh, yes, yes. But, you know, Basie used to tell me years ago, he had so many things he used to say, 'You can't play on a full stomach,' you know. You don't give

a good performance, you know. And for years, well, I figured I was only making $6.00 a night, and he was always so big and fat, you know. So for years he had me psyched out, that you couldn't eat -- you couldn't play on a full stomach.
So one day I happened to eat just before I went on the bandstand. Ate a good meal and I played -- gee whiz, I never felt so good.

I didn't know why he stayed so fat, you know. And I gave him hell, "You want to tell me something like that?" You know. But I finally found out -- well, you find out for yourself years later what's good for you. And you do what's good for you.
Well, that could be true, couldn't it, for some people?
Yes, lot of people, you know, they can't perform on a full stomach. But I can. Because I went without a full stomach by request with Basie for a long time. We weren't making any money.
